problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v$ at time $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Velocity for Plane Motion Using Differentiation

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨4\sqrt{1+t},(1+t)^{2}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v$ at time $t=3.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\sqrt{1+t}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((1+t)^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2(1+t)^{-1/2},2(1+t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{\sqrt{1+t}},2+2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=3,$ we substitute into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =⟨\frac{2}{\sqrt{1+3}},2+2(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{2},\,2+6⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
